_comment: Example spec. Replace with your own; this file is illustration, not data.
Every entry cites the page it came from in `source`, which lands in the
event description so an event on a phone can be traced back to the page
that claimed it. Only add a date a source actually states — if a date is
TBD, leave it out rather than guessing. A wrong date on a calendar is
worse than a missing one, because you plan around it.
`key` is the stable identity used for reconciliation. Keep it stable and a
changed date MOVES the event; change the key and you get a second event.
`color` is a category from colors.py. State it explicitly where the shape
of the work matters: inference reads words, and it cannot tell that a
course hackathon is teaching load rather than coursework.

events.title: Project 2 due
events.notes: 15% of grade. Group. Late days shared across projects.

events.title: Student deadline — first build due
events.notes: Course staff view: expect a support surge the day before.

events.title: Hackathon (evening, whole cohort)
events.notes: Staffed evening. This is teaching load, not coursework — which is why the color is stated rather than inferred.
